_about: The editor's rulebook: every number the Mac editor and the phone editor share. yaplib/rules.py reads it on the Mac; the Anima app reads the same file on the phone, bundled and refreshed from this repo. Change a value here, release, and both editors cut the same way. Values that only one surface uses stay in that surface's code. Seconds end in _s, decibels in _db.

cut._about: yapcut.py. Why each rule exists is in the yapcut.py docstring and CHANGELOG 2.3.

word_gaps._about: 3.8.1: a pause the envelope cannot see (wind, fans, room tone as loud as the voice) is cut where the take's own word transcript and a window re-transcription both hear no speech. 3.9.0: on a take whose voice sits mic_separation_db over the room tone, a candidate as loud as the voice (within mic_veto_under_voice_db) is dropped words, never cut; a candidate whose cut would remove under cut.min_cut_s is not confirmed.

captions._about: build_ass.py. `preset` is the live one; the others are kept for --preset.

hook._about: The burned hook. Word limits are gates.sh; fit and animation are build_ass.py. The fitter shrinks every author line toward min_size before it wraps one. minimal draws lines after the first at sub_frac, and build_ass draws outline instead when a later line is longer than line 1. shadow_ass_alpha is the ASS alpha byte: 0 opaque, 255 clear.

retention._about: retention_check.py via gates.sh. Joins the cutter made do not count as events.

dead_air._about: gap_check.py via gates.sh: pauses that survived the cut. mic_separation_db: when the voice sits this far over the cut's quietest frames the microphone measures each pause itself and no whisper runs (3.9.0); a frame more than pause_under_voice_db under the voice is a pause.

edit_record._about: finalize.sh writes <name>.edit.json; the phone writes the same shape so log_perf.py --edits joins either.

repetition._about: The repetition gate. acoustic: yaplib/repeats.py finds the same audio twice (a ridge of MFCC self-similarity at one lag) and the cross-window scan decodes whisper windows only there (3.9.0). windows: the short windows xwin_scan.py decodes around each candidate.
